why:
phase-482 W4 (2026-10-07): `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode` IS an `rclcpp::Node`, so this is `rclcpp::Node::count_publishers`, inherited, with `cpp:Node::count_publishers`'s contract. The extractor records only the members a class declares, so this key correlates as upstream-only even though the name resolves.

Before phase-482 W4: LANDED 2026-09-04 (phase-417 stage 2b): `nros::Node` and `nros::LifecycleNode` now forward this to the executor that owns them (`node.hpp`, `rclcpp_lifecycle/lifecycle_node.hpp`), over FFI that already shipped on `nros::Executor` (`executor.hpp:205-301`). It was verdicted `gap` -- not implemented -- when the capability was present one type over and only the forwarder was missing.

It stays a divergence on SHAPE. rclcpp returns owned heap containers (`std::vector<std::string>`, `std::map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>>`); the graph has no bound a caller can know, so a caller-sized buffer is an unanswerable question and an owned container needs an allocator. Ours streams through a visitor, which costs one entry of peak RAM.

ADOPT-BOUNDED envelope (RFC-0089), stated in the header: the call reports what has been DISCOVERED and never blocks, so an empty result means "nobody seen yet", not "nobody exists"; a backend with no graph returns `Unsupported`, which is a different answer from empty and must not be collapsed into zero.
